description.value: The study investigated emotion regulation and its neural correlates in euthymic bipolar disorder type I patients and healthy controls using a full 2 × 2 factorial fMRI paradigm with instruction and valence factors.

spans.text: Therefore, we decided to study ER and its neural correlates in a group of euthymic BD-I patients using a well-validated functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) paradigm that avoided previous limitations.

description.value: A full 2 × 2 factorial event-related design with valence (Negative/Neutral) and instruction (Look/Decrease) as within-subject factors and group (BD/HC) as the between-subjects factor.

spans.text: Critically, we employed a full 2 × 2 factorial event-related design, which allowed us to identify brain activations specifically associated with negative emotion downregulation, by orthogonalizing the valence (Negative/Neutral) and instruction (Look/Decrease) factors.

value: Active comorbid disorder associated with bipolar I disorder at testing; personality disorder; alcohol or drug abuse or dependence during the last year; benzodiazepine use; standard MRI contraindications including claustrophobia, metallic implants, or pregnancy.

spans.text: Exclusion criteria were the presence of any major Axis I psychiatric disorder (control group) or the presence at the time of testing of an active co-morbid disorder associated to the diagnosis of bipolar I disorder (bipolar group). The presence of any personality disorder was also an exclusion criterion in both groups. Other exclusion criteria included a history of alcohol or drug abuse or dependence during the last year, use of benzodiazepines, as well as standard exclusion criteria for MRI scanning (e.g. claustrophobia, metallic implants, pregnancy).

The ER task was based on the ‘situational focused strategy’.

description.value: Participants viewed negative or neutral images under Look or Decrease instructions; Decrease trials required reappraisal to downregulate negative affect.

spans.text: A picture depicting either a negative or neutral scene was then presented for 10 s, followed by a 7-point rating scale in which participants rated how much negative affect they felt during the presentation of the previous image.

The paradigm was similar to that used in previous studies (Ochsner et al. Reference Ochsner, Bunge, Gross and Gabrieli 2002 , Reference Ochsner, Ray, Cooper, Robertson, Chopra, Gabrieli and Gross 2004 ), and consisted of a full 2 × 2 factorial design, with valence (Negative/Neutral) and instruction (Look/Decrease) as within-subject orthogonal factors.

instructions.value: For Look trials, passively view the picture and let emotions flow spontaneously. For Decrease trials, decrease negative affect through situationally focused reappraisal by imagining that the event will have a positive outcome.

spans.text: Each trial started with a 10-s fixation cross, followed by a cue (4 s) instructing subjects to either look at the following picture letting their emotions flow spontaneously or decrease the negative affect induced by it through reappraisal.

stimuli.value: Forty-eight negative and 48 neutral images from the International Affective Pictorial System; 16 images per category were presented in each of two equivalent sessions.

spans.text: A total of 48 negative and 48 neutral images selected from the International Affective Pictorial System (IAPS) were used in the experiment.
